protections: Classification of non-global / IPv4-carrying IPv6 ranges: the TYPES table read by getType() (src/v6/constants.ts:25-53, src/ipv6.ts:567-576, src/ipv6.ts:1472-1475) plus the boolean predicates isMapped4 / isTeredo / is6to4 / isLoopback / isULA / isMulticast / isLinkLocal / isUnspecified / isDocumentation (src/ipv6.ts:1203-1293).

Decoding of the IPv4 address embedded in IPv6 forms so IPv4 policy can be re-applied: to4() (src/ipv6.ts:894-910), toAddress4Nat64()/fromAddress4Nat64() (src/ipv6.ts:1048-1116), inspect6to4() (src/ipv6.ts:1002-1016), inspectTeredo() (src/ipv6.ts:937-995).
Special-purpose IPv4 classification: isPrivate / isLoopback / isLinkLocal / isCGNAT / isBroadcast / isUnspecified / isMulticast (src/ipv4.ts:456-506).
The shared subnet-membership primitive isInSubnet that every range classifier is built on (src/common.ts:9-19).

traps.what: Both NAT64 prefixes exist only as getType string labels; no boolean NAT64 predicate exists, so a caller filtering on predicates cannot ask whether an address is NAT64 at all (well-known or local-use).
traps.reason_to_dismiss: getType() already returns 'NAT64 (well-known)' and 'NAT64 (local-use)' for these ranges (src/v6/constants.ts:51-52) and the pinned tests assert exactly that (test/functionality-v6-test.ts:87-93), so the range looks recognised and a predicate seems redundant.

traps.what: isMulticast(), isLoopback(), isUnspecified() and getScope() decide on the getType() string, and TYPES has no ::ffff:0:0/96 (or 2001::/32) entry, so IPv4-mapped addresses are reported as ordinary 'Global unicast' by the predicates that proxy through the type label.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: isMapped4() already checks the ::ffff:0:0/96 bits directly (src/ipv6.ts:1243-1245, IPV4_MAPPED_SUBNET at src/ipv6.ts:1480) and isTeredo() covers 2001::/32, so the range looks handled and the type table looks like a display-only concern.

traps.what: isLinkLocal() compares the first 64 bits against fe80:0:0:0 while getType() uses the fe80::/10 entry, so the two implementations of the same property disagree for addresses in fe80::/10 that are not inside fe80::/64.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The in-code comment at src/ipv6.ts:1204 asserts that zeroes are required and that isInSubnet with 'fe80::/10' cannot be used, which reads as a deliberate decision, and getType() already returns 'Link-local unicast' for the same addresses via src/v6/constants.ts:47.

traps.what: isInSubnet() returns false whenever the address's own prefix is shorter than the checked prefix, so a host address that carries a shorter CIDR suffix is treated as outside ranges it actually belongs to, and every classifier built on isInSubnet inherits that shape.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The short-circuit is the correct meaning of subnet containment (a /8 is not inside a /9) and is pinned by test/functionality-v6-test.ts:250-260; host addresses with a prefix are documented as valid (src/ipv6.ts:156-162, src/ipv4.ts:46-52, README.md:44-48), and request targets do not normally carry a CIDR suffix, so the shape looks irrelevant to a security check.

traps.what: Address4.isPrivate() recognises only the three RFC 1918 blocks, so the other special-purpose IPv4 ranges are not 'private' by that predicate even though the class also offers separate loopback, link-local, CGNAT, broadcast and unspecified checks.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The docstring and README define isPrivate as RFC 1918 only (src/ipv4.ts:461, README.md:151) and the neighbouring predicates isLoopback/isLinkLocal/isCGNAT/isBroadcast/isUnspecified already exist (src/ipv4.ts:472-506), so the narrow scope reads as intentional API design.

traps.what: The IPv4-compatible ::/96 form (::a.b.c.d) is parsed into v4 groups but is neither in the TYPES table nor inside isMapped4()'s ::ffff:0:0/96 constant, so that notation is classified as ordinary global unicast.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: IPv4-compatible addressing is deprecated (RFC 4291 section 2.5.5.1) and most stacks only map ::ffff:0:0/96, so the omission reads as deliberate scope, reinforced by the test that lists '::1.2.3.4' in the isMapped4 reject set (test/functionality-v6-test.ts:1118) and by the 'we can't match addresses like ::192.168.0.1 yet' note (test/address-test.ts:81).

traps.what: toAddress4Nat64() defaults to the well-known /96 prefix and returns null outside it, and the local-use /48 decoding uses the RFC 6052 split around bits 64-71 rather than the trailing-32-bit rule, so the default decode path yields nothing for the local-use range.
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The default prefix is documented as the well-known 64:ff9b::/96 (src/ipv6.ts:1084, README.md:226) and pinned by the test at test/functionality-v6-test.ts:446-449; a null return is the documented contract, and callers can pass '64:ff9b:1::/48' explicitly.

masking: T7 becomes visible only once T1 is fixed: after a NAT64 predicate exists, a caller who then relies on the no-argument toAddress4Nat64() still gets null for a local-use address (src/ipv6.ts:1089-1099), so classification without extraction gives false assurance.

Fixing T2 changes getScope()/isMulticast() results for ::ffff:0:0/96 addresses and exposes that the multicast branch keys on the getType() string (src/ipv6.ts:540-546) rather than on the multicast bit pattern.

conflicts.what: Relaxing the isInSubnet prefix short-circuit (the natural T4 fix) would change documented subnet-containment results pinned by test/functionality-v6-test.ts:250-260 while making a prefixed host such as '64:ff9b:1::1/32' a NAT64 member; T1 therefore has to be fixed with a dedicated bit predicate, not by widening the shared primitive.

Auto-detecting the NAT64 prefix inside toAddress4Nat64() must keep the documented well-known default (README.md:226, test/functionality-v6-test.ts:446-449) and the six RFC 6052 prefix-length vectors (test/functionality-v6-test.ts:423-444); the T1 fix cannot route local-use addresses through the trailing-32-bit path of to4() (src/ipv6.ts:894-910), which decodes a /48 local-use address to 0.0.x.y.

fairness_risks: Broadening Address4.isPrivate() (T5) contradicts its documented RFC 1918 meaning (README.md:151) and silently changes results for callers who use it as exactly that predicate.

Any NAT64 fix must preserve the documented well-known defaults of fromAddress4Nat64()/toAddress4Nat64() (src/ipv6.ts:1041, src/ipv6.ts:1084, README.md:191, README.md:226) and the six RFC 6052 test vectors (test/functionality-v6-test.ts:423-444).

Rejecting prefix-bearing host strings to close T4 would break input that isValid() explicitly documents as legitimate (src/ipv4.ts:46-52, src/ipv6.ts:156-162, README.md:44-48) and that subnet arithmetic legitimately produces.

Widening isLinkLocal() to fe80::/10 must keep fe80::/64 addresses true and must not disturb getScope()'s Link local path for fe80::/10 or its Global answer for 2002::/16 (test/functionality-v6-test.ts:49-55).
Adding a ::ffff:0:0/96 entry to TYPES changes the public getType() string for mapped addresses, which consumers may be keying on as 'Global unicast' (the default return at src/ipv6.ts:575).

design.why: The five sit in four different layers and each has a different reason to dismiss it: T1 is an absent predicate hidden behind a getType label that already names the range, T2 is a proxy-object decision (isLoopback/isMulticast/isUnspecified delegate to a type table with no mapped entry) hidden behind the existence of isMapped4(), T3 is a second implementation that disagrees with the type table and is defended by an in-code comment, T4 is a shared-primitive shape (prefix-bearing hosts) whose dismissal is the correct subnet-containment semantics, and T7 is a defaults/RFC 6052 shape where the natural fix collides with the documented default. Together they include the advisory's own route (T1, T7) plus three sibling gaps with independent fix sites, so a solver who only adds a NAT64 predicate, or only edits one file, leaves the others open; T4 and T7 are the mimo-type how/coupled-value mechanisms and T1/T2/T3 are the deepseek-type absent-with-dismissal mechanisms.

unverified: The exact public API that B's fix adds is not visible in the pinned tree (b_fix ab3dc88bcf53 is not an ancestor of e82a681). getType() already labels 64:ff9b:1::/48 (src/v6/constants.ts:52, asserted at test/functionality-v6-test.ts:92), so the residual gap recorded in T1/T7 is inferred to be the predicate/decoder layer (e.g. an isNAT64-style helper and the no-argument decode default) rather than the type table.

A's fix diff (4a1f613f4c1b) and B's fix diff are not present in the worktree, so which lines A authored, and therefore whether B is an incomplete fix or a regression, is inferred from the presence of isMapped4()/toAddress4Nat64()/the NAT64 TYPES labels and cannot be verified from this checkout.
Exploitability of T4 and T6 depends on the downstream consumer and OS routing behavior; the library-level classification gap is verified from source, the end-to-end SSRF route is not reproduced here.

Whether the hidden behavioural tests exercise prefix-bearing host strings (T4), the IPv4-compatible ::/96 form (T6), or IPv4-mapped loopback via isLoopback() (T2) is unknown; those traps are recorded from the pinned code, not from the advisory text.
No git history or network access was used, so published dates and the wording of the two advisories were not re-checked beyond the supplied candidate record.
